A cold night, a call to mercy

It was an ordinary night in a hotel room, and a question would not let the founder sleep: What is the meaning of my life? What was I here to give?

He stepped outside with that question unanswered. Near the hotel stood a thin dog, shivering against a wall, looking for any shelter from the cold. In that forgotten creature he felt a quiet sign from God.

He fed the dog and stayed until he settled. Back in his room, he slept for the first time in a long while without the question hanging over him. He finally had a direction.

One person feeding one dog changes one night. So he opened an Instagram page and a WhatsApp group, and invited others to stand with him. People answered, and they showed up every day.

If I could not walk past this one dog and pretend I hadn’t seen him, then maybe my purpose was simply this: to stop pretending I hadn’t seen.

What Islam teaches us about mercy

“There is no creature on earth, nor bird that flies with its wings, but that they are communities like you.”Qur’an 6:38
“Whoever is not merciful to others will not be treated mercifully.”Prophet Muhammad ﷺ, Sahih al-Bukhari

The thirsty dog

A man gave water to a dying, thirsty dog, and Allah forgave his sins for this act of mercy. There is a reward for kindness to every living creature.

The woman and the cat

A woman was punished for locking up a cat until it died of hunger, neither feeding it nor releasing it to find food.

Worship, not sentiment

Feeding a stray is worship in our tradition. Mercy to the smallest creature is never a small deed.

Awareness sessions

We hold sessions in neighborhoods, colleges, community halls and schools, with one message every time: animals feel pain, animals feel fear, and animals deserve the mercy we hope for ourselves.

400+

people have heard our message directly in awareness sessions held in neighborhoods, colleges and community halls. Some now feed a street dog on their way to work. Some report cruelty instead of walking past.

We are still a young community. Four hundred is not a ceiling. It is a beginning.

The dog who disturbed no one

In loving memory. A story from Hyderabad, Sindh, shared by Rabeet Naeem Khanzada.

For four years Rabeet fed and watched over a gentle dog who lived near her home, the calmest she had ever known. She never troubled a neighbor and never asked for more than a little food and a little kindness. In September, Rabeet travelled to Karachi. When she returned, her dog had been poisoned.

She never disturbed anyone. She never harmed anyone. She lived quietly, and she was loved.“Indeed, we belong to Allah, and indeed, to Him we shall return.” Qur’an 2:156

Rabeet has never been a silent witness. She raises her voice for animal rights because animals cannot speak for themselves. A true animal activist, and a true human being.

Our agenda: helping animals

Everything we do returns to one simple agenda. This is what we ask of ourselves, and what we invite you to join.

  1. Feed and shelter strays in your own street, every single day.
  2. Rescue and treat injured or sick animals without delay.
  3. Speak up and report cruelty whenever you witness it.
  4. Host or attend awareness sessions in your community.
  5. Teach children early that mercy to animals is mercy to all.
  6. Treat this as an act of faith, not a favor to be praised for.

Looking ahead

We hope for more feeding points, more rescue capacity, more awareness sessions, and more young people who choose compassion as a habit, not an event.

We dream of a day when no dog shivers unnoticed outside a building full of people, and every one of those people has somewhere to turn.

The road has not been easy

There are more animals in need than hands to help them. There are nights we could not save one we tried hard to save. But every hard night has been outweighed by one wagging tail, one recovered stray, one more person who decided to care.

A word from the founder

I am not a scholar. I am not a veterinarian. I am simply a man who, one ordinary night, asked himself an extraordinary question, and an animal answered it for me.

This is not about me. It is about a dog shivering outside a hotel, a WhatsApp group that grew into a family, and more than four hundred people who decided that mercy should not be optional.

To those seeking to adopt: I will always arrange pets for you. This community is my family.

Jahangeer Ejaz Zehri

Founder, The Animal Welfare Network
